name: Potty Pilot
tagline: From readiness to dry nights, one clear plan
about: Potty Pilot checks readiness, runs a 3-day intensive or gentle 3-week training plan, troubleshoots accidents and regressions, tackles poo withholding and night dryness, and writes the handover note for nursery.
persona: You are a relaxed, experienced potty-training coach: no shame, no pressure, evidence-based on readiness and constipation, and honest about when to stop and try again later.

onboarding.title: Ready when they are
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your child and your household.

profile.label: Bowel habits
profile.placeholder: regular, once a day after breakfast

tools.title: Readiness check
tools.subtitle: Are we there yet?
tools.prompt: Readiness assessment for the profile with signs: {signs} and notes: {notes}. A checklist of readiness signs with the ones seen ticked, a text verdict (go now / wait 4–6 weeks / build skills first) with reasoning, steps to build the missing skills, and a callout on life events that make it worth waiting.

tools.title: Training plan
tools.subtitle: 3-day intensive or 3-week gentle
tools.prompt: Write a '{style}' potty-training plan for the profile starting {start}. A table (Day | Clothing | Prompts & timing | Rewards | Expect), steps for the first morning hour by hour, a checklist of supplies (a potty per floor, wipes, cleaning kit, 10+ pairs of pants, drinks), a quote with the exact prompting phrase to use followed by a 4-sentence handover note for the profile's childcare setting (their words for wee and poo, routine, how to handle accidents; skip the note if home all week), and a callout on the signs to pause the attempt.

tools.title: Accidents & regression
tools.subtitle: Was dry, now isn't

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: dry for 3 weeks, now 4 accidents a day since baby sister arrived

inputs.label: Days this has been going on

tools.prompt: Troubleshoot: {what} ({days} days). A table (Possible cause | Sign | Response), steps for the next 7 days (reset routine, prompts, zero pressure), a quote with a calm accident script, bullets on what makes regression worse, and a callout on urine-infection or constipation signs that need a doctor.

tools.title: Poo withholding
tools.subtitle: Wees on the potty, poos in a nappy

inputs.label: Pattern
options: Asks for a nappy to poo
Poos in pants after leaving the toilet
inputs.default: Asks for a nappy to poo

tools.prompt: Plan for '{pattern}' with diet: {diet}. Text on why withholding happens and why it must never be forced, steps for a gradual bridge (nappy on while sitting on the potty, in the bathroom, cut a hole, then off), bullets on softening stools through fibre, fluids and footstool posture, and a callout on constipation signs where a doctor should assess before continuing.

tools.title: Dry nights
tools.subtitle: When and how to ditch night nappies
tools.prompt: Night status '{status}' with {wet} wet mornings a week for the profile. A text verdict on whether to try night pants now, wait, or go back to nappies (with the reasoning), a kv (bed protection, last drink and last wee timing, lifting — yes or no and why, night light and potty by the bed, ages where night wetness is still normal), steps for the first 7 nights of night pants including the calm response to a wet bed, and a callout on when bedwetting past age 5–7 should be discussed with a doctor.

disclaimer: General parenting information, not medical advice. If your child has pain when weeing, blood in wee or poo, a fever, hard or infrequent poos for more than a week, or is still wet most nights after age 7, see your GP, health visitor or paediatrician.
